parameters.name: uone
parameters.description: `uone = 60` U_1 is a round input scale chosen before fitting, comparable to the training input magnitude, solely for conditioning; it is not a fitted threshold.

parameters.name: utwo
parameters.description: `utwo = 20` U_2 is a round input scale chosen before fitting, comparable to the training input magnitude, solely for conditioning; it is not a fitted threshold.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Feedback magnitude, jointly fitted; see expression for whether it multiplies a state difference or a dimensionless logarithm.

parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Dimensionless first-input feedback modifier or sigmoid location, as specified by the expression.

parameters.name: ybase
parameters.description: Fitted reference state, not assumed to be an independently measured physical equilibrium.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Magnitude of the second-input forcing at normalized input unity.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Dimensionless fitted exponent of the nonnegative normalized second input.

estimation.criterion: Minimize the unweighted sum of squared simulated-minus-logged `y` residuals at every post-initial sample in each complete trajectory. This matches the evaluation objective and was selected by the internal suffix simulation comparison.
estimation.data: Final parameter estimation uses every derivative row of data/train.csv and data/val.csv as two separate trajectories. Where rollout residuals enter, it also uses all states after the first of each trajectory. Initial structural searches fitted data/train.csv only and compared free-running simulation on data/val.csv. A subsequent criterion comparison fitted the full training file plus zero-based validation rows 0 through 727 and evaluated rows 728 through 1453, with an independent measured initialization at row 728. The suffix was then included in the final refit to use all supplied identification information. No test data were accessed. No rows were discarded in the final fit.
estimation.method: The preliminary training derivative fit used bounded trust-region reflective nonlinear least squares, scipy.optimize.least_squares, from three deterministic numerical start vectors (`k = 0.14999999999999999`, `g = 0.55000000000000004`, `ybase = 1`, `source = 0.01`, `n = 2`); (`k = 0.10707380931422739`, `g = 0.44697975120483147`, `ybase = 1.0787876713600761`, `source = 0.0089518267441960047`, `n = 2.2102464818070038`); (`k = 0.17421970870228037`, `g = 0.39121154728704011`, `ybase = 1.2034127577784375`, `source = 0.00880870270493001`, `n = 2.8376339943610551`). These were generated in the exploratory search with numpy random seed 15; the best derivative SSE solution initialized later fits. Bounds for the preliminary and final model were `k` in `[0.0001, 5]` 1/s; `g` in `[-5, 5]` -; `ybase` in `[0.69999999999999996, 1.3]` U_y; `source` in `[0, 0.5]` U_y/s; `n` in `[0.20000000000000001, 8]` -. They are numerical identification constraints allowing broad reference states and positive source/exponent/rate, not supplied physical information. The final solution does not reach these bounds. The final solver starts were `k = 0.1825662048339487`, `g = 0.66589578083130163`, `ybase = 0.99053265125297207`, `source = 0.011543120627838252`, `n = 1.7118218481938601`, taken from affine_rate derivative in nonlinear_results.json because the prior derivative fit was already in a reasonable local basin. Final and criterion-comparison fits use scipy.optimize.least_squares with trust-region reflective, `x_scale = "jac"`, maximum 800 function evaluations, and dimensionless tolerances `ftol = 1e-10`, `xtol = 1e-10`, `gtol = 1e-10`. Nonlinear least squares supports the free-running residual criterion, for which a linear coefficient solve is not available. No random numbers enter this final step. Criterion selection compared derivative-only least squares, rollout-only least squares, and joint least squares with derivative residuals multiplied by `10*sqrt(w)` s for dimensionless trial weights `w = 1` and `w = 10`. The 10 s residual scale is a chosen conditioning/tradeoff scale, not an identified time constant. The criterion with smallest suffix rollout RMSE was selected. Every rollout uses classical RK4 with 5 s steps, logged inputs held constant, and a single first-state initialization, never later measured-state resets. All fitted parameters are jointly reestimated at each fitting stage; intermediate estimates are not frozen.

discussion.family: Bilinear-in-state/input continuous-time model with power-law additive input forcing. General nonlinear-model reference: O. Nelles, Nonlinear System Identification, Springer, 2001 (bibliographic reference recalled from memory, not externally checked).
discussion.interpretation: The state `y`, inputs `x1` and `x2`, and target `dy` are the logged columns. Their physical units are unknown. `U_y`, `U_1` and `U_2` below denote unspecified native units of `y`, `x1` and `x2`; `dy` has units `U_y/s`. In `-k*(1-g*(x1/uone))*(y-ybase)+source*Max(x2/utwo,0)**n`, `-k*(y-ybase)` is linear state feedback and `k*g*(x1/uone)*(y-ybase)` opposes it as the first input rises. The second-input power term is additive forcing. For a fixed input, the state dynamics are affine; negative effective feedback rates are possible above the inferred crossing. The nonnegative input extension avoids complex fractional powers; it is not identified by negative-input data.
discussion.origin: Quadratic polynomial fitting and backward elimination revealed a dominant product of the first input and the state deviation. A compact model retaining that interaction and a fitted second-input power was therefore proposed by mathematical simplification, not physical inference. The reference state and power exponent were allowed to vary instead of fixing the baseline or forcing it to be quadratic. In the internal criterion comparison, the best suffix rollout RMSE was 0.057390959 U_y on rows 728 through 1453 of data/val.csv, initialized only at row 728 (zero-based rows). This suffix was excluded from that fitting stage but had already been inspected in exploratory validation, so this is not a pristine independent estimate. After refitting on both complete files, the training and validation rollout RMSE values are 0.032981244 and 0.041078753 U_y; these final values are in-sample, not unseen-data scores. Final predicted-minus-logged derivative residual lag-one correlations are 0.572954 and 0.518603 (dimensionless) on training and validation, respectively.
discussion.limitations: There is no supplied physical description or intended use; no term is assigned a physical mechanism. This is a scalar autonomous-in-state, memoryless-in-input approximation, not evidence that omitted dynamics are absent. It cannot represent input histories, disturbances or time-dependent hidden states. Observed derivative residual correlation motivated nonlinear feedback and input-rate interactions, but remained after these extensions. Sampled derivatives need not be exact continuous-time derivatives, and integration-method effects are absorbed into fitted values. Extrapolation beyond the sampled state/input ranges is unverified; uncertainty intervals were not estimated. The affine rate is not restricted to remain positive, so persistent first inputs beyond the fitted crossing can produce exponential growth.
